records.context: Annotation is the bottleneck in every screen. An extracted image region the model already calls with 0.999 teaches the model nothing when a human labels it; the extracted image regions worth a person's afternoon are the ones sitting on the decision boundary. This module turns an already-scored ``measurements.db`` into a work list ordered so the informative extracted image regions come first.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Annotation is the bottleneck in every screen. A crop the model already calls with 0.999 teaches the model nothing when a human labels it; the crops worth a person's afternoon are the ones sitting on the decision boundary. This module turns an already-scored ``measurements.db`` into a work queue ordered so the informative crops come first.
records.translation: A anotação é o gargalo de toda triagem. Um recorte que o modelo já classifica com 0.999 não ensina nada ao modelo quando uma pessoa o rotula; os recortes que valem a tarde de alguém são os que estão sobre a fronteira de decisão. Este módulo transforma um ``measurements.db`` já pontuado em uma fila de trabalho ordenada de modo que os recortes informativos venham primeiro.

records.context: **Uncertainty sampling skews toward the majority class.** On a screen that is 98 % negative, the decision boundary is mostly populated by negatives, so the annotation work list will be too. The annotation work list summary reports this as a class-balance table so the annotator can cap or rebalance the annotation work list.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Uncertainty sampling skews toward the majority class.** On a screen that is 98 % negative, the decision boundary is mostly populated by negatives, so the queue will be too. The queue summary reports this as a class-balance table so the annotator can cap or rebalance the queue.
records.translation: **A amostragem por incerteza tende para a classe majoritária.** Em uma triagem 98 % negativa, a fronteira de decisão é povoada principalmente por negativos, e a fila também será. O resumo da fila informa isso como uma tabela de equilíbrio de classes, para que o anotador possa limitar ou reequilibrar a fila.

records.context: **A softmax is not a probability.** Everything here is called an uncertainty *score*, never a confidence. Modern networks are badly calibrated — typically over-confident, and more so the deeper they are (Guo et al., 2017) — so a 0.87 from the head is not "87 % sure". The scores are used for one thing only: putting extracted image regions in an order. Nothing in this module reports a calibrated probability, and neither should anything built on it. See :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A softmax is not a probability.** Everything here is called an uncertainty *score*, never a confidence. Modern networks are badly calibrated — typically over-confident, and more so the deeper they are (Guo et al., 2017) — so a 0.87 from the head is not "87 % sure". The scores are used for one thing only: putting crops in an order. Nothing in this module reports a calibrated probability, and neither should anything built on it. See :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.
records.translation: **Um softmax não é uma probabilidade.** Tudo aqui é chamado de *pontuação* de incerteza, nunca de confiança. As redes modernas são mal calibradas — tipicamente confiantes demais, e tanto mais quanto mais profundas (Guo et al., 2017) —, de modo que um 0.87 vindo da cabeça não significa "87 % sure". As pontuações servem para uma única coisa: colocar os recortes em uma ordem. Nada neste módulo informa uma probabilidade calibrada, e nada construído sobre ele deveria fazê-lo. Consulte :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.

records.context: **Already-annotated extracted image regions never enter the annotation work list.** ``NULL`` in the annotation column is the abstention marker — the extracted image region has not been looked at. ``0`` is a real class, and an annotation work list that re-serves it wastes exactly the resource this module exists to save. The two are distinguished by ``IS NULL``, never by falsiness. (Same convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)
records.label: spacr.active_learning#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Already-annotated crops never enter the queue.** ``NULL`` in the annotation column is the abstention marker — the crop has not been looked at. ``0`` is a real class, and a queue that re-serves it wastes exactly the resource this module exists to save. The two are distinguished by ``IS NULL``, never by falsiness. (Same convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)
records.translation: **Recortes já anotados nunca entram na fila.** ``NULL`` na coluna de anotação é o marcador de abstenção — o recorte não foi examinado. ``0`` é uma classe real, e uma fila que o reapresenta desperdiça exatamente o recurso que este módulo existe para poupar. Os dois são distinguidos por ``IS NULL``, nunca pela avaliação como falso. (Mesma convenção de :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)

records.context: **The two head shapes are handled separately.** The machine-learning classification model head emits either a single logit (binary; needs a sigmoid) or C logits (multiclass; needs a softmax) — see :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Pushing a single-logit column through a softmax yields a column of 1.0 and destroys the ordering; pushing C logits through a sigmoid can *invert* it. Both are silent failures that produce a confident-looking work list full of nonsense, so :func:`probabilities_from_logits` branches on the shape and the tests pin both directions.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The two head shapes are handled separately.** The classifier head emits either a single logit (binary; needs a sigmoid) or C logits (multiclass; needs a softmax) — see :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Pushing a single-logit column through a softmax yields a column of 1.0 and destroys the ordering; pushing C logits through a sigmoid can *invert* it. Both are silent failures that produce a confident-looking queue full of nonsense, so :func:`probabilities_from_logits` branches on the shape and the tests pin both directions.
records.translation: **Os dois formatos de cabeça são tratados separadamente.** A cabeça do classificador emite um único logit (binário; requer uma sigmoide) ou C logits (multiclasse; requer um softmax) — consulte :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Passar uma coluna de logit único por um softmax produz uma coluna de 1.0 e destrói a ordenação; passar C logits por uma sigmoide pode *invertê-la*. Ambas são falhas silenciosas que produzem uma fila de aparência confiável cheia de absurdos, por isso :func:`probabilities_from_logits` ramifica pelo formato e os testes fixam as duas direções.

records.source: The distribution of labels across experimental units determines whether a classifier can generalize beyond acquisition-specific staining, focus and confluency. A label set concentrated within one well can therefore yield optimistic performance under an object-level random split. This function exposes such concentration before model training or evaluation.
records.translation: A distribuição dos rótulos entre as unidades experimentais determina se um classificador consegue generalizar além da coloração, do foco e da confluência específicos de uma aquisição. Um conjunto de rótulos concentrado em um único poço pode, portanto, produzir um desempenho otimista sob uma divisão aleatória por objeto. Esta função expõe essa concentração antes do treinamento ou da avaliação do modelo.

records.source: The measures above see one model's opinion and call a 50/50 output "uncertain" whether the model is genuinely torn or merely mis-calibrated. records.translation: As medidas acima veem a opinião de um único modelo e chamam uma saída 50/50 de "uncertain", seja o modelo genuinamente dividido ou apenas mal calibrado. records.context: ``(N,)`` or ``(N, 1)`` — a **single-logit binary head**. Sigmoid, then expanded to ``[1 − p, p]`` so every measure sees two classes. Pushing this through a softmax instead would return a column of 1.0 — every extracted image region maximally certain, the whole ordering gone.

records.translation: ``(N,)`` ou ``(N, 1)`` — uma **cabeça binária de logit único**. Sigmoide, depois expandida para ``[1 − p, p]`` para que toda medida veja duas classes. Passar isto por um softmax retornaria uma coluna de 1.0 — todos os recortes com certeza máxima, e toda a ordenação perdida.

records.context: ``(N, C)`` with C ≥ 2 — a **C-logit head**. Row-wise softmax. Sigmoiding these instead reads each logit in isolation and can invert the order: ``[5, 5]`` is a perfect 50/50 tie under softmax but looks like a confident 0.993 under a sigmoid of column 1.

records.translation: 1. ajusta um modelo a todos os rótulos em ``annotation_column``; 2. o avalia em uma divisão reservada **agrupada**, para que o número não seja um artefato de 190 rótulos vindos de um único poço; 3. grava de volta as probabilidades por classe em ``png_list`` como colunas :data:`ROUND_PRED_PREFIX`, que :func:`build_queue` prefere à coluna ``pred`` mais antiga — de modo que a próxima fila é genuinamente reordenada; 4. registra a rodada, dando a :func:`learning_curve` mais um ponto; 5. retorna o :class:`StoppingVerdict` da curva até agora.

Because pooled screens do not identify which individual cell contains a guide, the result represents cells whose measured phenotype is consistent with the fitted effect; it does not assign a genotype to individual cells. :class:`MontagePlan` includes :data:`INFERENCE_NOTICE` in every generated caption to preserve this distinction.
records.translation: A entrada consiste em um coeficiente no nível de guia ou de gene, medições por objeto e frações de guias por poço. Como as triagens agrupadas não identificam qual célula individual contém uma guia, o resultado representa células cujo fenótipo medido é consistente com o efeito ajustado; não atribui um genótipo a células individuais. :class:`MontagePlan` inclui :data:`INFERENCE_NOTICE` em toda legenda gerada para preservar essa distinção.

records.context: Selection proceeds in three stages:
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Selection proceeds in three stages:
records.translation: A seleção ocorre em três etapas:

records.context: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifies microplate sample positions with a non-zero fraction of the guide or gene. Gene-level selection sums guide fractions by default; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evaluates guides separately. 2. :func:`score_window` defines ``target = baseline + effect`` and retains objects within ``half_widths`` robust scales of the target, ordered by ``|score - target|``. The baseline and scale are calculated across the supplied object population rather than separately for each gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selects ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objects from each microplate sample position. Zero-contribution microplate sample positions remain in the plan for reporting.
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifies wells with a non-zero fraction of the guide or gene. Gene-level selection sums guide fractions by default; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evaluates guides separately. 2. :func:`score_window` defines ``target = baseline + effect`` and retains objects within ``half_widths`` robust scales of the target, ordered by ``|score - target|``. The baseline and scale are calculated across the supplied object population rather than separately for each gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selects ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objects from each well. Zero-contribution wells remain in the plan for reporting.
records.translation: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifica os poços com fração não nula da guia ou do gene. A seleção no nível de gene soma as frações das guias por padrão; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` avalia as guias separadamente. 2. :func:`score_window` define ``target = baseline + effect`` e retém os objetos a até ``half_widths`` escalas robustas do alvo, ordenados por ``|score - target|``. A linha de base e a escala são calculadas sobre a população de objetos fornecida, e não separadamente para cada gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` seleciona ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objetos de cada poço. Os poços sem contribuição permanecem no plano para fins de relatório.

records.context: This module converts vendor image files into a layout spaCR can read. It is **decoupled from the mask workflow**: nothing here imports torch, cellpose or :mod:`spacr.core`, so it can be executed, tested and previewed on a laptop with no GPU and no segmentation settings in sight.
records.label: spacr.convert#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module converts vendor image files into a layout spaCR can read. It is **decoupled from the mask pipeline**: nothing here imports torch, cellpose or :mod:`spacr.core`, so it can be run, tested and previewed on a laptop with no GPU and no segmentation settings in sight.
records.translation: Este módulo converte arquivos de imagem de fabricantes em uma estrutura que o spaCR consegue ler. Ele é **desacoplado do pipeline de máscaras**: nada aqui importa torch, cellpose ou :mod:`spacr.core`, de modo que pode ser executado, testado e visualizado previamente em um notebook sem GPU e sem nenhuma configuração de segmentação à vista.

records.context: **Z that is not silently flattened.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` max-projects unconditionally in three of its four branches (ND2, LIF, and both the 3-D and 4-D TIFF cases), and says so nowhere in its output. Here the default is :data:`Z_KEEP` — every image layer is written with its own ``Z##`` — and choosing to project is an explicit ``z_handling='max'``, announced in the plan and recorded per row in the map file.
records.label: spacr.convert#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Z that is not silently flattened.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` max-projects unconditionally in three of its four branches (ND2, LIF, and both the 3-D and 4-D TIFF cases), and says so nowhere in its output. Here the default is :data:`Z_KEEP` — every plane is written with its own ``Z##`` — and choosing to project is an explicit ``z_handling='max'``, announced in the plan and recorded per row in the map file.
records.translation: **Z que não é achatado silenciosamente.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` faz projeção máxima incondicionalmente em três dos seus quatro ramos (ND2, LIF e ambos os casos de TIFF 3-D e 4-D), e não diz isso em lugar algum da sua saída. Aqui o padrão é :data:`Z_KEEP` — cada plano é gravado com o seu próprio ``Z##`` —, e optar pela projeção é um ``z_handling='max'`` explícito, anunciado no plano e registrado por linha no arquivo de mapa.

records.context: Design rules
records.label: spacr.convert#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Design rules
records.translation: Regras de design

records.context: **No new required dependencies.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` are probed with :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; when one is missing the affected files are reported as skipped with the package name and the ``pip install`` line, never as an ImportError traceback.
records.label: spacr.convert#12
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **No new required dependencies.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` are probed with :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; when one is missing the affected files are reported as skipped with the package name and the ``pip install`` line, never as an ImportError traceback.
records.translation: **Nenhuma nova dependência obrigatória.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` são sondados com :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; quando um deles está ausente, os arquivos afetados são informados como ignorados, com o nome do pacote e a linha de ``pip install``, nunca como um traceback de ImportError.

records.context: **Never overwrite.** Two sources landing on one target name is a *plan-time error* naming both, not a last-writer-wins at convert time. An output that already exists on disk is skipped and counted, so a repeat execution is a no-op rather than a silent rewrite.
records.label: spacr.convert#13
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Never overwrite.** Two sources landing on one target name is a *plan-time error* naming both, not a last-writer-wins at convert time. An output that already exists on disk is skipped and counted, so a re-run is a no-op rather than a silent rewrite.
records.translation: **Nunca sobrescreve.** Duas fontes que caem no mesmo nome de destino constituem um *erro no momento do planejamento* que nomeia ambas, e não um "o último a gravar vence" no momento da conversão. Uma saída que já existe em disco é ignorada e contada, de modo que uma nova execução não faz nada em vez de regravar silenciosamente.

records.context: **Atomic writes.** Every TIFF is written to a temp file in the destination and :func:`os.replace`\ d into place, so an interrupted run leaves no half-written file that the next run mistakes for done.
records.label: spacr.convert#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Atomic writes.** Every TIFF is written to a temp file in the destination and :func:`os.replace`\ d into place, so an interrupted run leaves no half-written file that the next run mistakes for done.
records.translation: **Gravações atômicas.** Cada TIFF é gravado em um arquivo temporário no destino e colocado no lugar com :func:`os.replace`, de modo que uma execução interrompida não deixa nenhum arquivo gravado pela metade que a execução seguinte confunda com um arquivo concluído.

records.context: **Ledgered.** A conversion that skipped 12 unreadable files says so in one grouped block at the end and stamps ``conversion_map.run_status.json`` next to its output — see :mod:`spacr.errors`.
records.label: spacr.convert#15
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Ledgered.** A conversion that skipped 12 unreadable files says so in one grouped block at the end and stamps ``conversion_map.run_status.json`` next to its output — see :mod:`spacr.errors`.
records.translation: **Com registro.** Uma conversão que ignorou 12 arquivos ilegíveis o informa em um único bloco agrupado no final e grava ``conversion_map.run_status.json`` ao lado da sua saída — consulte :mod:`spacr.errors`.

records.context: :func:`spacr.io.convert_to_yokogawa` already converts ND2/CZI/LIF/TIFF, and it is still the right tool when you want an in-place rename of a flat folder. It does not provide the three features of this module:

records.source: :func:`spacr.io.convert_to_yokogawa` already converts ND2/CZI/LIF/TIFF, and it is still the right tool when you want an in-place rename of a flat folder. It does not provide the three features of this module:

records.context: **Preview.** It writes as it walks. There is no point at which you can look at "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" and say no. :func:`plan` produces that table and writes nothing.

records.source: **Preview.** It writes as it walks. There is no point at which you can look at "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" and say no. :func:`plan` produces that table and writes nothing.
records.translation: **Visualização prévia.** Ele grava à medida que percorre. Não há nenhum momento em que se possa olhar para "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" e dizer não. :func:`plan` produz essa tabela e não grava nada.

records.context: **A map you can read back.** It writes a ``rename_log.csv`` whose columns differ per input format (the LIF and TIFF branches record two columns; the ND2 branch records seven; the CZI branch records nine), and nothing in spaCR ever reads it. :func:`write_map` emits one fixed schema and :func:`read_map` / :func:`populate_db_from_map` read it back, so after a run the original filename for any measurement is one SQL join away.

records.source: **A map you can read back.** It writes a ``rename_log.csv`` whose columns differ per input format (the LIF and TIFF branches record two columns; the ND2 branch records seven; the CZI branch records nine), and nothing in spaCR ever reads it. :func:`write_map` emits one fixed schema and :func:`read_map` / :func:`populate_db_from_map` read it back, so after a run the original filename for any measurement is one SQL join away.
records.translation: **Um mapa que pode ser lido de volta.** Ele grava um ``rename_log.csv`` cujas colunas diferem conforme o formato de entrada (os ramos LIF e TIFF registram duas colunas; o ramo ND2 registra sete; o ramo CZI registra nove), e nada no spaCR jamais o lê. :func:`write_map` emite um único esquema fixo, e :func:`read_map` / :func:`populate_db_from_map` o leem de volta, de modo que, após uma execução, o nome de arquivo original de qualquer medição está a uma junção SQL de distância.

records.source: The rule, in full:
records.translation: A regra, por completo:

records.context: All three are deterministic — the same folder names always produce the same microplate sample positions — and step 3 is only *reversible* because the map file records ``source_well`` next to ``well``. After conversion ``plate1_A01`` cannot be traced to its folder without the map, so :func:`plan` also reports every synthetic assignment by name.
records.label: spacr.convert.assign_wells#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: All three are deterministic — the same folder names always produce the same wells — and step 3 is only *reversible* because the map file records ``source_well`` next to ``well``. After conversion ``plate1_A01`` cannot be traced to its folder without the map, so :func:`plan` also reports every synthetic assignment by name.
records.translation: As três são determinísticas — os mesmos nomes de pasta sempre produzem os mesmos poços —, e a etapa 3 só é *reversível* porque o arquivo de mapa registra ``source_well`` ao lado de ``well``. Após a conversão, ``plate1_A01`` não pode ser rastreado até a sua pasta sem o mapa, por isso :func:`plan` também informa cada atribuição sintética pelo nome.

records.context: This used to be a private ``^([A-Pa-p])[ _\-]?(\d{1,2})$`` with an extra ``1 <= column <= 24`` check, so ``Q01`` (row 17) and ``A25`` (column 25) — both perfectly good microplate sample positions of the 1536-laboratory microplate the heatmap already draws — came back None and were *renamed* to the next free synthetic address. :func:`spacr.schema.parse_well` is now the parser, and :func:`spacr.schema.plate_format_for` decides whether the position it produced is a microplate sample position that exists.

records.source: This used to be a private ``^([A-Pa-p])[ _\-]?(\d{1,2})$`` with an extra ``1 <= column <= 24`` check, so ``Q01`` (row 17) and ``A25`` (column 25) — both perfectly good wells of the 1536-plate the heatmap already draws — came back None and were *renamed* to the next free synthetic address. :func:`spacr.schema.parse_well` is now the parser, and :func:`spacr.schema.plate_format_for` decides whether the position it produced is a well that exists.
records.translation: Antes, isto era um ``^([A-Pa-p])[ _\-]?(\d{1,2})$`` privado com uma verificação extra ``1 <= column <= 24``, de modo que ``Q01`` (linha 17) e ``A25`` (coluna 25) — ambos poços perfeitamente válidos da placa de 1536 que o mapa de calor já desenha — voltavam como None e eram *renomeados* para o próximo endereço sintético livre. :func:`spacr.schema.parse_well` é agora o analisador, e :func:`spacr.schema.plate_format_for` decide se a posição que ele produziu é um poço que existe.

Image Lab stores ``zero_is="white"`` data, so such an image is inverted as ``data_ceiling - raw``; the result then looks like Image Lab's own PDF and TIFF exports (dark objects on a light background). ``zero_is="black"`` data is returned as stored.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Pure numpy and the standard library: the file is a MIME multipart document whose ``ScanImageTagN`` parts each hold raw ``ImageData`` (width x height uint16 in the stated endianness) and an XML ``ImageHeader``. Image Lab stores ``zero_is="white"`` data, so such an image is inverted as ``data_ceiling - raw``; the result then looks like Image Lab's own PDF and TIFF exports (dark objects on a light background). ``zero_is="black"`` data is returned as stored.
records.translation: Apenas numpy e a biblioteca padrão: o arquivo é um documento MIME multipart cujas partes ``ScanImageTagN`` contêm cada uma ``ImageData`` bruto (largura x altura em uint16 na ordem de bytes declarada) e um ``ImageHeader`` XML. O Image Lab armazena dados ``zero_is="white"``, por isso uma imagem assim é invertida como ``data_ceiling - raw``; o resultado então se parece com as próprias exportações em PDF e TIFF do Image Lab (objetos escuros sobre fundo claro). Dados ``zero_is="black"`` são retornados como armazenados.

records.context: 1. the registry knows it — anything unregistered is never a candidate; 2. its kind is not an **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): nothing in :mod:`spacr.ports` declares that it produces raw images or sequencing reads, so nothing can make them again; 3. a declared **producing module** exists for its kind, and the module the registry recorded is one of them; 4. that module's **inputs are complete** — every recorded input artifact is still registered and still on disk, and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` says the module could execute in this project right now; 5. it was written by a processing session that **finished** (``status == "complete"``); 6. what is on disk still **fingerprints to what was registered**, so a folder somebody has since dropped a file into is not prunable; 7. it lives **inside the project**, reached without following a symlink; 8. **every** artifact sharing its path passes all of the above — three kinds live in ``measurements.db``, and deleting the file for one of them destroys the other two; 9. no other registered artifact sits inside it or around it, because the bytes belong to the innermost one and a plan must not under-report what it deletes.
records.label: spacr.data_manager#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. the registry knows it — anything unregistered is never a candidate; 2. its kind is not an **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): nothing in :mod:`spacr.ports` declares that it produces raw images or sequencing reads, so nothing can make them again; 3. a declared **producing module** exists for its kind, and the module the registry recorded is one of them; 4. that module's **inputs are complete** — every recorded input artifact is still registered and still on disk, and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` says the module could run in this project right now; 5. it was written by a run that **finished** (``status == "complete"``); 6. what is on disk still **fingerprints to what was registered**, so a folder somebody has since dropped a file into is not prunable; 7. it lives **inside the project**, reached without following a symlink; 8. **every** artifact sharing its path passes all of the above — three kinds live in ``measurements.db``, and deleting the file for one of them destroys the other two; 9. no other registered artifact sits inside it or around it, because the bytes belong to the innermost one and a plan must not under-report what it deletes.
records.translation: 1. o registro o conhece — nada que não esteja registrado é candidato; 2. o seu tipo não é um **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): nada em :mod:`spacr.ports` declara que produz imagens brutas ou leituras de sequenciamento, portanto nada pode recriá-las; 3. existe um **módulo produtor** declarado para o seu tipo, e o módulo que o registro anotou é um deles; 4. as **entradas desse módulo estão completas** — cada artefato de entrada registrado continua registrado e em disco, e :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` diz que o módulo poderia ser executado neste projeto agora mesmo; 5. foi gravado por uma execução que **terminou** (``status == "complete"``); 6. o que está em disco ainda **tem a mesma impressão digital que foi registrada**, de modo que uma pasta na qual alguém colocou um arquivo desde então não pode ser removida; 7. está **dentro do projeto**, alcançado sem seguir um link simbólico; 8. **todos** os artefatos que compartilham o seu caminho passam em todas as condições acima — três tipos ficam em ``measurements.db``, e excluir o arquivo de um deles destrói os outros dois; 9. nenhum outro artefato registrado está dentro dele ou em torno dele, porque os bytes pertencem ao mais interno, e um plano não pode subestimar o que exclui.

records.context: Rule 3 also protects other kinds. ``ports.producers_of`` is empty for ``raw-images`` and ``sequencing-reads``, which is *why* originals are safe — and it is empty today for ``channel-stacks`` too, so ``stack/`` is reported as unregistered bytes and never offered, even though it is one of the largest intermediates. This changes only when a port declares that it produces them.

records.source: Rule 3 also protects other kinds. ``ports.producers_of`` is empty for ``raw-images`` and ``sequencing-reads``, which is *why* originals are safe — and it is empty today for ``channel-stacks`` too, so ``stack/`` is reported as unregistered bytes and never offered, even though it is one of the largest intermediates. This changes only when a port declares that it produces them.
records.translation: A regra 3 também protege outros tipos. ``ports.producers_of`` é vazio para ``raw-images`` e ``sequencing-reads``, e é *por isso* que os originais estão seguros — e hoje também é vazio para ``channel-stacks``, de modo que ``stack/`` é informado como bytes não registrados e nunca é oferecido, embora seja um dos maiores intermediários. Isso só muda quando uma porta declarar que os produz.

records.context: Nothing is deleted without a plan.  :func:`plan_prune` returns exactly what would go and how much it frees; :func:`prune` refuses to run unless it is handed :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, a digest over that exact path set and byte total, so a confirmation cannot authorise a deletion other than the one that was shown.

records.source: Nothing is deleted without a plan.  :func:`plan_prune` returns exactly what would go and how much it frees; :func:`prune` refuses to run unless it is handed :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, a digest over that exact path set and byte total, so a confirmation cannot authorise a deletion other than the one that was shown.
records.translation: Nada é excluído sem um plano.  :func:`plan_prune` retorna exatamente o que sairia e quanto espaço isso libera; :func:`prune` se recusa a executar a menos que receba :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, um resumo sobre exatamente esse conjunto de caminhos e esse total de bytes, de modo que uma confirmação não pode autorizar uma exclusão diferente da que foi exibida.

records.context: Deleting is **count first, delete second, verify**. The tree is re-fingerprinted against the plan before anything is removed; the registry write is a count and a write on one predicate, checked for equality and rolled back on any difference. See :func:`_verified_write`.
records.label: spacr.data_manager#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Deleting is **count first, delete second, verify**. The tree is re-fingerprinted against the plan before anything is removed; the registry write is a count and a write on one predicate, checked for equality and rolled back on any difference. See :func:`_verified_write`.
records.translation: A exclusão segue **contar primeiro, excluir depois, verificar**. A árvore tem a impressão digital recalculada e comparada com o plano antes que qualquer coisa seja removida; a gravação no registro é uma contagem e uma gravação sobre um único predicado, verificadas quanto à igualdade e revertidas em caso de qualquer diferença. Consulte :func:`_verified_write`.

Any difference — a file added, a file changed, the folder gone — aborts the whole call before a single delete; 3. the registry write happens next, inside one transaction, counted and verified (see :func:`_verified_write`). A mismatch rolls it back and raises with **nothing on disk deleted**; 4. only then are the files removed; 5. every path is checked to be gone afterwards.
records.translation: 1. a confirmação deve ser igual a :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, um resumo sobre os caminhos exatos e o total de bytes do plano, de modo que um token não pode autorizar uma exclusão diferente daquela para a qual foi exibido; 2. cada candidato tem a impressão digital recalculada e ainda deve corresponder ao plano. Qualquer diferença — um arquivo acrescentado, um arquivo alterado, a pasta desaparecida — aborta a chamada inteira antes de uma única exclusão; 3. a gravação no registro acontece em seguida, dentro de uma única transação, contada e verificada (consulte :func:`_verified_write`). Uma divergência a reverte e gera exceção com **nada excluído em disco**; 4. só então os arquivos são removidos; 5. depois, verifica-se que cada caminho desapareceu.

records.context: ``ari`` — **background is excluded.** The Adjusted Rand Index over two raw label images is dominated by background: a 1400x1400 microscope field of view is ~95 % background, both models agree it is background, and those agreed pairs swamp everything else. Two models that disagree about every single object still score about 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` asserts exactly that number on a microscope field of view where the foreground agreement is 0.0).
records.label: spacr.model_compare#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``ari`` — **background is excluded.** The Adjusted Rand Index over two raw label images is dominated by background: a 1400x1400 field is ~95 % background, both models agree it is background, and those agreed pairs swamp everything else. Two models that disagree about every single object still score about 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` asserts exactly that number on a field where the foreground agreement is 0.0).
records.translation: ``ari`` — **o fundo é excluído.** O Índice de Rand Ajustado sobre duas imagens de rótulos brutas é dominado pelo fundo: um campo de 1400x1400 tem ~95 % de fundo, os dois modelos concordam que é fundo, e esses pares concordantes sobrepujam todo o resto. Dois modelos que discordam sobre cada objeto ainda pontuam cerca de 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` verifica exatamente esse número em um campo onde a concordância de primeiro plano é 0.0).

records.context: So the index is computed over the **union foreground** — the pixels at least one model assigned to an object — with pixels the *other* model left unassigned treated as unclustered singletons rather than as one big background cluster. With background as a single cluster, a model that misses an entire object still scores 1.0, because "one object plus a background blob" and "one object plus a background blob" are the same partition. As singletons, missing half the objects scores 0.50.
records.label: spacr.model_compare#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: So the index is computed over the **union foreground** — the pixels at least one model assigned to an object — with pixels the *other* model left unassigned treated as unclustered singletons rather than as one big background cluster. With background as a single cluster, a model that misses an entire object still scores 1.0, because "one object plus a background blob" and "one object plus a background blob" are the same partition. As singletons, missing half the objects scores 0.50.
records.translation: Por isso o índice é calculado sobre o **primeiro plano da união** — os pixels que pelo menos um modelo atribuiu a um objeto —, com os pixels que o *outro* modelo deixou sem atribuição tratados como singletons não agrupados, em vez de como um grande agrupamento de fundo. Com o fundo como um único agrupamento, um modelo que perde um objeto inteiro ainda pontua 1.0, porque "one object plus a background blob" e "one object plus a background blob" são a mesma partição. Como singletons, perder metade dos objetos pontua 0.50.

records.context: Computed in closed form from the object overlap matrix (see :func:`adjusted_rand_index`) rather than by materialising millions of singleton labels; ``tests/test_model_compare.py`` checks it against ``sklearn.metrics.adjusted_rand_score`` on the expanded arrays.

records.source: ARI is a *pixel-pair* index, so it is sensitive to boundaries and it is degenerate when a field holds one object (a single cluster has no pair structure to agree about). It is reported next to the object-level numbers for that reason, never alone.
records.translation: O ARI é um índice de *pares de pixels*, por isso é sensível às bordas e é degenerado quando um campo contém um único objeto (um único agrupamento não tem estrutura de pares sobre a qual concordar). Por esse motivo é informado ao lado dos números no nível de objeto, nunca sozinho.

records.context: ``iou_matched_fraction`` and ``mean_matched_iou`` — from an **optimal** assignment, not a greedy one. Matching objects between two segmentations is a bipartite assignment problem; picking each object's best partner double-assigns, and picking greedily in descending IoU can leave a pair stranded that an optimal assignment would have kept. Both failures are reproduced in the tests. :func:`match_objects` thresholds the IoU matrix and then runs :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` over it, which is also what ``cellpose.metrics`` does.
records.label: spacr.model_compare#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``iou_matched_fraction`` and ``mean_matched_iou`` — from an **optimal** assignment, not a greedy one. Matching objects between two segmentations is a bipartite assignment problem; picking each object's best partner double-assigns, and picking greedily in descending IoU can leave a pair stranded that an optimal assignment would have kept. Both failures are reproduced in the tests. :func:`match_objects` thresholds the IoU matrix and then runs :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` over it, which is also what ``cellpose.metrics`` does.
records.translation: ``iou_matched_fraction`` e ``mean_matched_iou`` — a partir de uma atribuição **ótima**, não gulosa. Fazer a correspondência de objetos entre duas segmentações é um problema de atribuição bipartida; escolher o melhor parceiro de cada objeto atribui em dobro, e escolher de forma gulosa em ordem decrescente de IoU pode deixar sem par um par que uma atribuição ótima teria mantido. As duas falhas são reproduzidas nos testes. :func:`match_objects` aplica um limiar à matriz de IoU e depois executa :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` sobre ela, que é também o que ``cellpose.metrics`` faz.

records.context: Above an IoU of 0.5 the assignment is provably unique — two objects cannot both overlap a third by more than half of it — so at the default threshold greedy would in fact get the same answer. The optimal assignment is used anyway because ``iou_threshold`` is a knob, and every value below 0.5 (which is where "roughly the same object" lives) makes greedy wrong.
records.label: spacr.model_compare#15
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Above an IoU of 0.5 the assignment is provably unique — two objects cannot both overlap a third by more than half of it — so at the default threshold greedy would in fact get the same answer. records.translation: Acima de um IoU de 0.5, a atribuição é comprovadamente única — dois objetos não podem ambos se sobrepor a um terceiro em mais da metade dele —, de modo que, no limiar padrão, o método guloso chegaria de fato à mesma resposta. A atribuição ótima é usada mesmo assim porque ``iou_threshold`` é ajustável, e todo valor abaixo de 0.5 (que é onde vive "roughly the same object") torna o método guloso errado.

records.context: A comparison that differs only in an argument the model never sees reports "no difference" and wastes the processing session. On the installed Cellpose 4, these are accepted and then dropped (see :data:`IGNORED_ARGUMENTS`): ``model_type``, ``diam_mean`` and ``nchan`` at construction, ``channels`` and ``rescale`` at ``eval``, plus spaCR's own ``restore_type``. Every pre-SAM model name resolves to ``cpsam`` too, so "cyto3 versus nuclei" is one model against itself.

records.source: A comparison that differs only in an argument the model never sees reports "no difference" and wastes the run. On the installed Cellpose 4, these are accepted and then dropped (see :data:`IGNORED_ARGUMENTS`): ``model_type``, ``diam_mean`` and ``nchan`` at construction, ``channels`` and ``rescale`` at ``eval``, plus spaCR's own ``restore_type``. Every pre-SAM model name resolves to ``cpsam`` too, so "cyto3 versus nuclei" is one model against itself.
records.translation: Uma comparação que difere apenas em um argumento que o modelo nunca vê informa "no difference" e desperdiça a execução. No Cellpose 4 instalado, estes são aceitos e depois descartados (consulte :data:`IGNORED_ARGUMENTS`): ``model_type``, ``diam_mean`` e ``nchan`` na construção, ``channels`` e ``rescale`` em ``eval``, além do próprio ``restore_type`` do spaCR. Todo nome de modelo pre-SAM também se resolve em ``cpsam``, de modo que "cyto3 versus nuclei" é um modelo contra si mesmo.

records.context: The index is taken over the pixels at least one mask assigned to an object. Pixels the other mask left unassigned stay in the sample but belong to no cluster (each is its own singleton), so a model that misses an object is penalised for it — with background as one shared cluster it would not be. Pixels neither mask claimed are dropped entirely: they are the agreement that would otherwise be the whole answer.
records.label: spacr.model_compare.adjusted_rand_index#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The index is taken over the pixels at least one mask assigned to an object. Pixels the other mask left unassigned stay in the sample but belong to no cluster (each is its own singleton), so a model that misses an object is penalised for it — with background as one shared cluster it would not be. Pixels neither mask claimed are dropped entirely: they are the agreement that would otherwise be the whole answer.
records.translation: O índice é calculado sobre os pixels que pelo menos uma máscara atribuiu a um objeto. Os pixels que a outra máscara deixou sem atribuição permanecem na amostra, mas não pertencem a nenhum agrupamento (cada um é o seu próprio singleton), de modo que um modelo que perde um objeto é penalizado por isso — com o fundo como um único agrupamento compartilhado, não seria. Os pixels que nenhuma máscara reivindicou são totalmente descartados: são a concordância que, caso contrário, seria a resposta inteira.

records.context: Computed in closed form from the object overlap table. Singleton clusters contribute nothing to any ``C(n, 2)`` term, so the expansion never has to be materialised; the only thing they change is the total pair count, which is taken over the union foreground.
records.label: spacr.model_compare.adjusted_rand_index#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Computed in closed form from the object overlap table. Singleton clusters contribute nothing to any ``C(n, 2)`` term, so the expansion never has to be materialised; the only thing they change is the total pair count, which is taken over the union foreground.
records.translation: Calculado em forma fechada a partir da tabela de sobreposição de objetos. Os agrupamentos singleton não contribuem para nenhum termo ``C(n, 2)``, de modo que a expansão nunca precisa ser materializada; a única coisa que eles alteram é a contagem total de pares, que é calculada sobre o primeiro plano da união.

records.context: Bipartite, not greedy. records.translation: Bipartida, não gulosa. Primeiro aplica-se um limiar à matriz de IoU (tudo abaixo de ``iou_threshold`` vira 0) e :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` então maximiza o IoU total sobre o que resta, que é o mesmo procedimento que ``cellpose.metrics._true_positive`` usa. Os dois casos são exercitados nos testes.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module is built around two properties of OME-NGFF.
records.translation: Este módulo é construído em torno de duas propriedades do OME-NGFF.

records.context: **1. The Spacing is built from the SPACE axes only.** A 5-d ngff image has axes ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: the time axis is in seconds, the image data channel axis has no unit at all, and z/y/x are in micrometers. A single ``Spacing`` over all five would have to answer "what unit is this?" with one string, and whatever it answered would be wrong for three of the axes — a stack whose spacing claims ``"um"`` while one of its axes steps in seconds passes the unit check in ``layers.py`` and is then drawn at the wrong scale. So :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` covers z/y/x, and t and c are reported alongside as :class:`Axis` records through :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` and :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nothing is lost; the reader does not treat seconds and micrometers as the same kind of number.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **1. The Spacing is built from the SPACE axes only.** A 5-D NGFF image has axes ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: the time axis is in seconds, the channel axis has no unit at all, and z/y/x are in micrometers. A single ``Spacing`` over all five would have to answer "what unit is this?" with one string, and whatever it answered would be wrong for three of the axes — a stack whose spacing claims ``"um"`` while one of its axes steps in seconds passes the unit check in ``layers.py`` and is then drawn at the wrong scale. So :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` covers z/y/x, and t and c are reported alongside as :class:`Axis` records through :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` and :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nothing is lost; the reader does not treat seconds and micrometers as the same kind of number.
records.translation: **1. O Spacing é construído apenas a partir dos eixos SPACE.** Uma imagem NGFF 5-D tem os eixos ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: o eixo de tempo está em segundos, o eixo de canal não tem unidade alguma, e z/y/x estão em micrômetros. Um único ``Spacing`` sobre os cinco teria de responder "what unit is this?" com uma única string, e qualquer resposta estaria errada para três dos eixos — uma pilha cujo espaçamento declara ``"um"`` enquanto um dos seus eixos avança em segundos passa na verificação de unidades em ``layers.py`` e é então desenhada na escala errada. Por isso :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` abrange z/y/x, e t e c são informados ao lado como registros :class:`Axis` por meio de :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` e :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nada se perde; o leitor não trata segundos e micrômetros como o mesmo tipo de número.

records.context: **2. Units are translated through an explicit table, and an unknown one is refused.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` is the mapping, written out. A unit that is not in it throws :class:`OmeZarrError`. It would be one line to default to ``"px"`` instead, and that one line is how a 0.65 µm pixel becomes a 0.65 px pixel and every downstream area comes out wrong by a factor of 10^6 — in a column named ``cell_area`` that still looks plausible. The error distinguishes the two cases that need different fixes: a unit NGFF does not define (the file is wrong), and a legal NGFF unit spaCR has no short token for (convert it, e.g. to ``micrometer``).

Uma unidade que não está nele gera :class:`OmeZarrError`. Seria uma linha usar ``"px"`` como padrão, e essa única linha é como um pixel de 0.65 µm se torna um pixel de 0.65 px e toda área calculada mais adiante sai errada por um fator de 10^6 — em uma coluna chamada ``cell_area`` que continua parecendo plausível. O erro distingue os dois casos que exigem correções diferentes: uma unidade que o NGFF não define (o arquivo está errado) e uma unidade NGFF válida para a qual o spaCR não tem token curto (converta-a, por exemplo para ``micrometer``).

It is never silently upgraded to µm, and ``"px"`` is never written out as a unit string, because NGFF has no pixel unit: writing a px spacing emits axes with no ``unit``, which is the same convention read back.

records.context: The writer builds a pyramid by **2x block mean over the two fastest-varying space axes** (see :func:`write_ome_zarr`). It is a box filter and **not a Gaussian pyramid**: there is no pre-filter beyond the box, so it aliases where a properly filtered pyramid would not. It is chosen anyway because it is separable, exact, dependency-free, and the same ``local_mean`` the rest of the NGFF ecosystem writes — matching what other viewers produce matters more here than a marginally better kernel. Striding (``downsample="stride"``) is offered and is **mandatory for label/mask arrays**: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, an object that does not exist.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#18
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The writer builds a pyramid by **2x block mean over the two fastest-varying space axes** (see :func:`write_ome_zarr`). It is a box filter and **not a Gaussian pyramid**: there is no pre-filter beyond the box, so it aliases where a properly filtered pyramid would not. It is chosen anyway because it is separable, exact, dependency-free, and the same ``local_mean`` the rest of the NGFF ecosystem writes — matching what other viewers produce matters more here than a marginally better kernel. Striding (``downsample="stride"``) is offered and is **mandatory for label/mask arrays**: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, an object that does not exist.
records.translation: O gravador constrói uma pirâmide por **média de blocos 2x sobre os dois eixos espaciais de variação mais rápida** (consulte :func:`write_ome_zarr`). É um filtro de caixa e **não uma pirâmide gaussiana**: não há pré-filtro além da caixa, de modo que produz aliasing onde uma pirâmide filtrada adequadamente não produziria. É escolhido mesmo assim porque é separável, exato, sem dependências e o mesmo ``local_mean`` que o resto do ecossistema NGFF grava — corresponder ao que outros visualizadores produzem importa mais aqui do que um kernel marginalmente melhor. A amostragem por passo (``downsample="stride"``) é oferecida e é **obrigatória para matrizes de rótulos/máscaras**: a média dos rótulos 3 e 5 é 4, um objeto que não existe.

records.context: Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's ``scale`` multiplied by the cumulative factor 2^k on each downsampled axis. Leaving it at level 0's value is a common NGFF bug — it renders as a pyramid whose coarse levels are a quarter the size of the fine ones and drift off the top-left corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and by a different rule per method: a block mean puts the first output element at the *centre* of the block it averaged, half a level-0 pixel in from the edge, so level *k* is translated by ``scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``; a strided level samples element 0 exactly and is not translated at all. Both are written, and asserted in the tests with the numbers spelled out by hand.

records.source: Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's ``scale`` multiplied by the cumulative factor 2^k on each downsampled axis. Leaving it at level 0's value is a common NGFF bug — it renders as a pyramid whose coarse levels are a quarter the size of the fine ones and drift off the top-left corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and by a different rule per method: a block mean puts the first output element at the *centre* of the block it averaged, half a level-0 pixel in from the edge, so level *k* is translated by ``scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``; a strided level samples element 0 exactly and is not translated at all. records.translation: O ``scale`` do nível *k* é o ``scale`` do nível 0 multiplicado pelo fator cumulativo 2^k em cada eixo subamostrado. Deixá-lo com o valor do nível 0 é um bug comum de NGFF — renderiza como uma pirâmide cujos níveis grosseiros têm um quarto do tamanho dos finos e se deslocam a partir do canto superior esquerdo à medida que se aplica zoom. O ``translation`` também se move, e por uma regra diferente para cada método: uma média de blocos coloca o primeiro elemento de saída no *centro* do bloco que calculou, meio pixel do nível 0 para dentro a partir da borda, de modo que o nível *k* é transladado por ``scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``; um nível por passo amostra exatamente o elemento 0 e não é transladado. Ambos são gravados e verificados nos testes com os números escritos à mão.

records.context: **Chunked.** The array is stored as a grid of independently compressed blocks, so a 100 GB plate is readable a tile at a time. Metadata queries read no array data: :func:`read_ome_zarr` opens a handful of small JSON files and returns the levels, their shapes, their voxel sizes and their chunk grids without reading any chunk, and :meth:`OmeZarrImage.read` with a ``region=`` decodes only the chunks that region intersects. Every byte of chunk data in the pure-Python path passes through one function, :func:`_read_chunk_bytes`, and ``tests/test_ome_zarr.py`` counts its calls to check that reads are lazy.

records.context: The **chunk codecs** are what need compiled code, so they are what the optional extra provides. This module decodes and encodes chunks compressed with ``zlib``, ``gzip``, ``bz2``, ``lzma`` or stored uncompressed using nothing but the standard library, which is why a spaCR-written OME-Zarr round-trips on a plain ``pip install spacr``. records.translation: Os **codecs de blocos** são o que exige código compilado, por isso são o que o extra opcional fornece. Este módulo decodifica e codifica blocos comprimidos com ``zlib``, ``gzip``, ``bz2``, ``lzma`` ou armazenados sem compressão usando apenas a biblioteca padrão, e é por isso que um OME-Zarr gravado pelo spaCR faz a viagem de ida e volta com um simples ``pip install spacr``. records.context: **The transformations.** Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's multiplied by 2^k on each downsampled axis — writing level 0's scale on every level is a common NGFF bug, and it renders as coarse levels that are a quarter the size of the fine ones and slide off the corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and differently per method: a block mean centres its first output element half a level-0 pixel inside the edge, so level *k* gets ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, while a strided level samples element 0 exactly and keeps ``translate_0``.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr.write_ome_zarr#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The transformations.** Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's multiplied by 2^k on each downsampled axis — writing level 0's scale on every level is a common NGFF bug, and it renders as coarse levels that are a quarter the size of the fine ones and slide off the corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and differently per method: a block mean centres its first output element half a level-0 pixel inside the edge, so level *k* gets ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, while a strided level samples element 0 exactly and keeps ``translate_0``.
records.translation: **As transformações.** O ``scale`` do nível *k* é o do nível 0 multiplicado por 2^k em cada eixo subamostrado — gravar a escala do nível 0 em todos os níveis é um bug comum de NGFF, e renderiza como níveis grosseiros com um quarto do tamanho dos finos que deslizam a partir do canto à medida que se aplica zoom. O ``translation`` também se move, e de forma diferente para cada método: uma média de blocos centraliza o seu primeiro elemento de saída meio pixel do nível 0 para dentro da borda, de modo que o nível *k* recebe ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, enquanto um nível por passo amostra exatamente o elemento 0 e mantém ``translate_0``.

records.context: Neither spaCRPower nor the port had this stage, and its absence is optimistic in a specific way: it makes the read fraction an *exact* measure of which genotypes were in a microplate sample position. In a real amplicon screening experiment it is not. A barcode arrives at the wrong gene through base-call substitutions, index hopping on a patterned flow cell, PCR chimeras across the pooled reaction, and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing — and every one of those mechanisms moves reads *toward the middle*, because the destination is drawn from the whole library rather than from the microplate sample positions the source genotype was actually in.

records.context: Mis-assignment gives a gene phantom reads in microplate sample positions it never entered, so the covariate the model regresses positive counts on is a shrunk-toward-uniform version of the truth. The obvious consequence is regression dilution — an attenuated coefficient and a smaller apparent effect — and measuring it in this simulator says that at realistic rates it is **small**: on the 452-gene reference design, 0.5 % mis-assignment moves the hit/non-hit separation from 0.799 to 0.794 among the genes that were identifiable to begin with. Deep sequencing averages most of it away.

records.source: Mis-assignment gives a gene phantom reads in wells it never entered, so the covariate the model regresses positive counts on is a shrunk-toward-uniform version of the truth. The obvious consequence is regression dilution — an attenuated coefficient and a smaller apparent effect — and measuring it in this simulator says that at realistic rates it is **small**: on the 452-gene reference design, 0.5 % mis-assignment moves the hit/non-hit separation from 0.799 to 0.794 among the genes that were identifiable to begin with. Deep sequencing averages most of it away.
records.translation: A atribuição errada dá a um gene leituras fantasmas em poços nos quais ele nunca entrou, de modo que a covariável sobre a qual o modelo regride as contagens positivas é uma versão da verdade encolhida em direção à uniforme. A consequência óbvia é a diluição da regressão — um coeficiente atenuado e um efeito aparente menor —, e medi-la neste simulador mostra que, em taxas realistas, ela é **pequena**: no delineamento de referência de 452 genes, 0.5 % de atribuição errada move a separação entre hits e não hits de 0.799 para 0.794 entre os genes que eram identificáveis desde o início. O sequenciamento profundo elimina a maior parte disso pela média.

records.context: The consequence that is *not* obvious, and is much larger, is what it does to the genes that were never testable. A gene that landed in every microplate sample position, or in none, has a constant read-fraction column; its coefficient is confounded with the intercept and ``power_model.prepare_model_data`` reports it as unidentified rather than as a non-hit. That check is what keeps a thin design from reporting untestable genes as negative results, and mis-assignment defeats it, because phantom reads give every gene a covariate that *varies*. On the same reference design, 0.5 % error takes the scored library from 317 genes to all 452: the 135 genes that were correctly flagged "untested" become scored non-hits with a covariate made entirely of noise, and the screening experiment-wide separation falls from 0.799 to 0.723 — fourteen times the direct dilution, and all of it from a safeguard being switched off rather than from any loss of signal.

records.source: The consequence that is *not* obvious, and is much larger, is what it does to the genes that were never testable. A gene that landed in every well, or in none, has a constant read-fraction column; its coefficient is confounded with the intercept and ``power_model.prepare_model_data`` reports it as unidentified rather than as a non-hit. That check is what keeps a thin design from reporting untestable genes as negative results, and mis-assignment defeats it, because phantom reads give every gene a covariate that *varies*. On the same reference design, 0.5 % error takes the scored library from 317 genes to all 452: the 135 genes that were correctly flagged "untested" become scored non-hits with a covariate made entirely of noise, and the screen-wide separation falls from 0.799 to 0.723 — fourteen times the direct dilution, and all of it from a safeguard being switched off rather than from any loss of signal.
records.translation: A consequência que *não* é óbvia, e é muito maior, é o que ela faz com os genes que nunca foram testáveis. Um gene que foi parar em todos os poços, ou em nenhum, tem uma coluna de fração de leituras constante; o seu coeficiente é confundido com o intercepto, e ``power_model.prepare_model_data`` o informa como não identificado, e não como não hit. Essa verificação é o que impede que um delineamento fraco informe genes não testáveis como resultados negativos, e a atribuição errada a anula, porque as leituras fantasmas dão a todo gene uma covariável que *varia*. No mesmo delineamento de referência, 0.5 % de erro leva a biblioteca pontuada de 317 genes para todos os 452: os 135 genes que estavam corretamente sinalizados como "untested" tornam-se não hits pontuados com uma covariável feita inteiramente de ruído, e a separação em toda a triagem cai de 0.799 para 0.723 — catorze vezes a diluição direta, e toda ela por causa de uma salvaguarda desativada, e não de qualquer perda de sinal.

records.context: The main reason to simulate this is therefore not the added noise: a screening experiment with sequencing error and a screening experiment without it disagree about *how many genes were tested*, and the count with error included is inflated.

records.context: **Where the under-dispersed case is approximate, and which way.** A binomial has an integer number of trials, so it cannot hit an arbitrary ``(mean, var)`` pair. Given the rounded ``n``, the success probability is set to ``mean / n`` so the **mean is exact** and the realised variance is ``mean * (1 - mean/n)``, the nearest value the family attains — within about ``1/n`` relative of the request. The mean is the one preserved because it is the biologically meaningful quantity (cells per well) and it sets the scale of everything downstream, whereas a variance off by a percent changes only how wide the well-to-well spread is. Rounding ``n`` while keeping ``p = (mean - var) / mean`` — the naive inversion — biases the *mean* instead, by up to half a count, which is a systematic error in every well of a sweep.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.sample_count_mean_variance#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Where the under-dispersed case is approximate, and which way.** A binomial has an integer number of trials, so it cannot hit an arbitrary ``(mean, var)`` pair. Given the rounded ``n``, the success probability is set to ``mean / n`` so the **mean is exact** and the realised variance is ``mean * (1 - mean/n)``, the nearest value the family attains — within about ``1/n`` relative of the request. The mean is the one preserved because it is the biologically meaningful quantity (cells per well) and it sets the scale of everything downstream, whereas a variance off by a percent changes only how wide the well-to-well spread is. Rounding ``n`` while keeping ``p = (mean - var) / mean`` — the naive inversion — biases the *mean* instead, by up to half a count, which is a systematic error in every well of a sweep.
records.translation: **Onde o caso subdisperso é aproximado, e em que direção.** Uma binomial tem um número inteiro de tentativas, por isso não consegue atingir um par ``(mean, var)`` arbitrário. Dado o ``n`` arredondado, a probabilidade de sucesso é definida como ``mean / n``, de modo que a **média é exata** e a variância obtida é ``mean * (1 - mean/n)``, o valor mais próximo que a família atinge — dentro de cerca de ``1/n`` em termos relativos da solicitação. A média é a preservada porque é a grandeza biologicamente significativa (células por poço) e define a escala de tudo o que vem depois, ao passo que uma variância errada em um por cento altera apenas a amplitude da dispersão entre poços. Arredondar ``n`` mantendo ``p = (mean - var) / mean`` — a inversão ingênua — enviesa, em vez disso, a *média*, em até meia contagem, o que é um erro sistemático em todos os poços de uma varredura.

records.context: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` controls how *even* the library is, and it runs the opposite way from intuition: large alpha gives every gene about ``1/n`` of the pool, alpha near zero concentrates the whole pool on one gene, and ``alpha = 1`` corresponds to a Gini index of 0.5. The real *T. gondii* screening experiment this simulator was fitted to came out at ``alpha = 0.6``, i.e. quite skewed — which is why some genes in it never reached enough microplate sample positions to be callable at all.

records.source: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` controls how *even* the library is, and it runs the opposite way from intuition: large alpha gives every gene about ``1/n`` of the pool, alpha near zero concentrates the whole pool on one gene, and ``alpha = 1`` corresponds to a Gini index of 0.5. The real *T. gondii* screen this simulator was fitted to came out at ``alpha = 0.6``, i.e. quite skewed — which is why some genes in it never reached enough wells to be callable at all.
records.translation: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` controla o quão *homogênea* é a biblioteca, e funciona no sentido oposto ao da intuição: um alpha grande dá a cada gene cerca de ``1/n`` do conjunto, um alpha perto de zero concentra o conjunto inteiro em um único gene, e ``alpha = 1`` corresponde a um índice de Gini de 0.5. A triagem real de *T. gondii* à qual este simulador foi ajustado resultou em ``alpha = 0.6``, ou seja, bastante assimétrica — e é por isso que alguns genes nela nunca chegaram a poços suficientes para serem sequer classificáveis.

records.context: Both imaging and sequencing plates originate from *one shared source*: the spot plate. Thus the genotypes in a well are one physical fact observed twice. Each stage uses an independent random stream. Changing the imaging-cell count therefore leaves sequencing draws unchanged. This separation allows meaningful comparison across a sweep of parameter values. Otherwise each point would also contain unrelated randomization.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.simulate_screen#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The imaging and sequencing plates are both simulated from the *same* spot plate — which genotypes are in a well is one physical fact, observed twice. Each stage draws from its own spawned child stream, so changing the number of imaging cells does not shift the sequencing draws; that independence is what makes a parameter sweep interpretable, since otherwise every point on the sweep would differ by an unrelated re-randomisation as well as by the parameter.
records.translation: As placas de imageamento e de sequenciamento são ambas simuladas a partir da *mesma* placa de distribuição — quais genótipos estão em um poço é um único fato físico, observado duas vezes. Cada etapa sorteia do seu próprio fluxo filho gerado, de modo que mudar o número de células imageadas não desloca os sorteios do sequenciamento; essa independência é o que torna interpretável uma varredura de parâmetros, já que, caso contrário, cada ponto da varredura diferiria por uma nova aleatorização sem relação, além de pelo parâmetro.

records.context: **Two departures from the R original, both deliberate.** Upstream computes ``n_reads_per_well = round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` inside a ``group_by(well)``, so ``nrow`` is the *library size*: with 452 genes and ``n_reads_total = 128318`` that is 284 reads per well, against a real screening experiment near 3e4. The parameter is documented as "total reads in the screening experiment" in one vignette and "geometric mean of well reads" in another. This function takes ``n_reads_per_well`` unambiguously and reports ``n_reads_total`` as the derived sum. Second, upstream's guard ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)`` is computed from ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)`` while the urn is ``round(cells * pcr)`` element-wise; the two differ by rounding and the draw can ask for more balls than the urn holds. The guard here is computed from the urn itself.

records.source: **Two departures from the R original, both deliberate.** Upstream computes ``n_reads_per_well = round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` inside a ``group_by(well)``, so ``nrow`` is the *library size*: with 452 genes and ``n_reads_total = 128318`` that is 284 reads per well, against a real screen near 3e4. The parameter is documented as "total reads in the screen" in one vignette and "geometric mean of well reads" in another. This function takes ``n_reads_per_well`` unambiguously and reports ``n_reads_total`` as the derived sum. Second, upstream's guard ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)`` is computed from ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)`` while the urn is ``round(cells * pcr)`` element-wise; the two differ by rounding and the draw can ask for more balls than the urn holds. The guard here is computed from the urn itself.
records.translation: **Dois desvios em relação ao original em R, ambos deliberados.** O original calcula ``n_reads_per_well = round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` dentro de um ``group_by(well)``, de modo que ``nrow`` é o *tamanho da biblioteca*: com 452 genes e ``n_reads_total = 128318``, isso dá 284 leituras por poço, contra cerca de 3e4 em uma triagem real. O parâmetro é documentado como "total reads in the screen" em uma vinheta e como "geometric mean of well reads" em outra. Esta função recebe ``n_reads_per_well`` sem ambiguidade e informa ``n_reads_total`` como a soma derivada. Em segundo lugar, a proteção original ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)`` é calculada a partir de ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)``, enquanto a urna é ``round(cells * pcr)`` elemento a elemento; os dois diferem pelo arredondamento, e o sorteio pode pedir mais bolas do que a urna contém. A proteção aqui é calculada a partir da própria urna.
